decisions.reason: ADRG page-8 and Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL identify the first treatment-emergent dermatologic record before ADTTE.ADT applies its strict-after test; the literal probe follows that selection and RFENDTC fallback. The five reported selected events occur on TRTSDT, so the literal excludes them while the alternative is justified by ADAE.TRTEMFL's inclusive condition and reproduces the reference.

The retained ADTTE.STARTDT section and raw MT.ADTTE.STARTDT name ADSL.RFSTDTC, a character field in published ADSL; its numeric date representation does not authorize a different source. adtte.yaml STARTDT reads ADSL.TRTSDT, whose upstream derivation uses EX_MINDTC/MIN(EX.EXSTDTC), not RFSTDTC through an intermediate.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT requires the event date to be nonmissing and after TRTSDT; adtte.yaml _IS_EVENT instead compares _EVDT <= _EOSDT. DERM_EV obtains treatment-emergent provenance through AOCC01FL, but neither that lookup nor another executable counterpart states the documented strict-after condition.
Define-XML ADTTE.ADT specifies conversion of ADSL.RFENDTC for the fallback without a death condition. adtte.yaml _EOSDT uses RFENDTC only for DCDECOD=DEATH and otherwise _DSSTDT from EOSDS.DSSTDTC.

Define-XML ADTTE.CNSR tests ADAE.TRTEMFL=Y for the first treatment-emergent dermatologic source described on ADRG page-8. adtte.yaml CNSR instead tests _IS_EVENT, which adds the _EVDT <= _EOSDT condition and the DERM_EV safety restriction.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCDOM identifies the domain used to populate ADT and limits it to ADAE or ADSL. adtte.yaml _DSSTDT reads EOSDS.DSSTDTC for the non-death fallback, yet SRCDOM reports ADSL, so the emitted provenance does not describe the executable source.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCVAR requires the variable used to populate ADT, naming ASTDT or RFENDT; ADSL.RFENDT exists and its retained method converts RFENDTC to a date. adtte.yaml non-death ADT instead comes from EOSDS.DSSTDTC through _DSSTDT/_EOSDT while SRCVAR reports RFENDT, so the actual fallback lineage differs.

The complete retained sections, including ADRG page-8 and Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL, state treatment-emergent dermatologic event selection without an ADAE.SAFFL restriction. The ADSL.SAFFL filter on ADRG page-13 selects the KM analysis population and does not document the additional source-event filter in adtte.yaml DERM_EV line 58.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT specifies ADSL.RFENDTC as the fallback, and no retained section states the EOSDS selection. The DSCAT condition, SCREEN FAILURE/FINAL LAB VISIT exclusions, and earliest DSSTDTC selection in adtte.yaml EOSDS lines 64-73 therefore lack a documented counterpart for ADT.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCDOM names the domain used for ADT, and ADTTE.ADT with ADAE.AOCC01FL and ADRG page-8 states the source selection and branch conditions. Failure to recover the actual lineage of fixed published ADT from equal date values is an observability limit of this isolated check, not an omitted source, condition or computation under CR-10.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCSEQ supplies AESEQ when SRCDOM=ADAE, while ADRG page-8 and ADAE.AOCC01FL supply first-treatment-emergent dermatologic provenance without a safety-flag filter. ADRG page-13 applies ADSL.SAFFL to display selection, not to the ADAE source rows, so DERM_EV line 58 adds an undocumented restriction.
